name: Suresh Krishna
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Suresh Krishna chairs the Chennai-based Sundram Fasteners, which makes components for the auto sector.
Krishna is the oldest member of the third generation of the storied T.V. Sundaram Iyengar family from the southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu.
Four families tied to the TVS Group restructured their cross-holdings, as per a 2020 agreement, which gave each family both ownership and control of their respective companies.
His eldest daughter Preethi has a board seat while two other daughters, Arathi and Arundathi, run the company.
forbes_facts: Krishna founded the company in 1966 as a small industrial unit in Ambattur, a suburb of Chennai city.
He studied literature in the U.S. and Germany.
Global clients of Sundram Fasteners include General Motors and Cummins.

name: Edouard Carmignac
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Edouard Carmignac founded Carmignac Gestion, one of Europe's largest asset managers, in 1989.
Carmignac owns 79% of the company, which now has about $40 billion in assets under management; employees and executives own the rest.
His daughter Maxime works at the company and is the heir apparent. His son directs Foundation Carmignac and another daughter, Lucrece, is an actress.
In 2019, Carmignac stepped back from managing Carmignac Patrimoine, which he had run since 1989. He is chairman and chief investment officer.
The Foundation Carmignac opened an exhibition space in 2018 to show nearly 300 art works on Porquerolles, an island off the South of France.
forbes_facts: Edouard Carmignac wanted to be a rock star but settled for finance after receiving a BA in economics from the University of Paris and an MBA from Columbia.
Carmignac is a keen polo player. His team reached the semi final of the prestigious Deauville Gold Cup in 2017.

name: Michael Chae
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Chae has served as chief financial officer of alternative asset management giant Blackstone since 2015. He was named vice chairman in January 2025.
Chae joined Blackstone in 1997 and ran its international private equity business before being tapped to oversee the firm's finances.
Chae previously worked at alternative asset manager The Caryle Group and investment bank Dillon, Read & Co.
Chae is an alum of Harvard, Yale and Cambridge. He is a director of the Harvard Management Company and founder of the Chae Initiative in Private Sector Leadership at Yale Law School.
He is also a member of the Council on Foreign Relations.

name: Riju Ravindran
appears_on: Hurun Global (2021-2023); Hurun India (2018-2019); Hurun Global U40 (2021)

name: Kuldip Rathee
forbes_bio: Kuldip Rathee chairs and runs New Delhi-based ASK Automotive, a manufacturer of auto components such as brakes for two-wheelers.
ASK Automotive  also makes brake disc pads and assemblies as well as safety control cables for speedometers and clutch assemblies.
Its list of clients includes TVS Motor Company, Hero MotoCorp, Suzuki, Yamaha and Royal Enfield.
It has 18 factories located across six Indian states.
His wife Vijay and sons Aman and Prashant sit on the company's board.
forbes_facts: He has a B.A. in economics from St. Stephen's College in Delhi.
In the 1970s he worked as a police officer for the Central Reserve Police Force, which is a federal body.

name: Diane Kemper
forbes_bio: Real estate heiress Diane Kemper is one of four Goldman siblings who co-own Solil Management, which owns at least 400 properties in New York City.
Trophies include retail and office space along Madison Avenue in midtown and high-end coops on the Upper East Side.
Diane is the second-oldest child of late patriarch Sol Goldman, who started buying up foreclosed properties for bargain prices in the 1950s.
Diane headed the residential leasing department for several decades. She scaled back due to health issues several years ago.
The family also owns a 17% stake in the World Trade Center developments in lower Manhattan.

name: Shao Zhongyi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2015-2017); Hurun Global (2014-2018); Hurun China (2009-2017)
forbes_bio: Shao Zhongyi chairs Shandong Sunrise Group,  the largest importer of soy in China.
Sunrise's business interests also include petroleum trading and processing.
A native of Rizhao in China's eastern Shandong province, Shao reportedly dropped out of junior high school to sell livestock feed.
Later, he allegedly bought out a bankrupt soybean crusher with help from his brother.

name: Yi Xianzhong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2024); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2007-2026)
forbes_bio: Yi Xianzhong chairs Bio-Thera Solutions, which develops drugs to treat tumors and cardiovascular and autoimmune diseases.
Bio-Thera listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange's Sci-Tech Innovation Board in February 2020.
Yi graduated from the South China University of Technology, where he majored in computers and radio.
He worked for a state-owned firm in Guangzhou after graduation before founding his first company, computer maker Hedy Computer.
Hedy, which went public in 2004, was acquired by Focus Media in 2016.

name: Li Weizhu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Hurun China (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Li Weizhu is the chairman and largest shareholder of Shenzhen-based gold jewelry retailer Zhou Liu Fu Jewellery.
Zhou Liu Fu is widely considered a clone of Chow Tai Fook Jewellery and Luk Fook Holdings, due to its name's similarity to those of its more established rivals.
With more than 4,000 shops in China, Zhou Liu Fu is the country's fifth largest jewelry chain by store count. Almost all of its shops are franchisees.
The company went public in a $165 million Hong Kong IPO in June 2025.
Li joined Zhou Liu Fu as a general manager in 2004, when his brother established the company with a friend. A year later, Li acquired all of the stake from his brother's friend.

name: Hur Young-in
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2016-2021); Hurun Global (2015-2019)
forbes_bio: Hur Young-in is chairman of the SPC Group, a holding company with interests in bakeries and fast-service restaurants.
Known as South Korea's "Franchise King," his company now has 1,800 Baskin-Robbins and Dunkin' Donut stores.
The SPC Group also runs Pascucci (Italian café), The World Vine (wine), Jamba Juice (smoothies) and New York burger house Shake Shack in Korea.
forbes_facts: His Paris Baguette, a bakery café franchise brand, now has more than 3,000 stores globally, mostly in South Korea.
Hur took over as CEO of his father's company, Samlip General Foods, famous for its Cream Bun, in 1981.

name: Hiroshi Okura
forbes_bio: Hiroshi Okura started cosmetics company Noevir Holdings in 1964 and is currently chairman, while his son, Takashi is president.
Okura says the products were inspired by a visit he made to Germany's Black Forest region.
The company implements an Avon-like direct-selling business model, and has subsidiaries in the U.S., Canada, China and Taiwan.
Noevir Holdings listed on the JASDAQ market in 2004 and on the First Section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange in 2012.
Noevir Holdings posted nearly $480 million in revenue in the fiscal year through September 2020.

name: Deng Hui
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020-2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2021); Hurun China (2019-2021)
forbes_bio: Deng Hui chairs ArcSoft, a supplier of software to the computer vision industry. Customers include Xiaomi, Sony and Intel.
Deng is a graduate of Washington University in St. Louis.
Deng worked as a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Cambridge before setting up his own business.
